issues.legal_issue: The six-year continuous-occupation requirement for a tenant seeking to purchase land is measured when the purchase application is made, not when the governing enactment commenced.
material_facts: Tenants applied to purchase land from their landlords, claiming continuous occupation for at least six years.
The landlords argued that the six years of continuous occupation had to be completed before the enactment commenced.
The dispute arose in applications and proceedings challenging the authorities’ treatment of tenants’ purchase claims.
issues.conclusion: A tenant satisfies the six-year requirement if the tenant has completed six years of continuous occupation by the date of the purchase application; the period need not have been completed when the enactment commenced, subject to the other applicable conditions.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 18(1)(i) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, the clause contains no requirement that six years of occupation be completed on the date the Act commenced. Read with section 18(1)(ii), which counts occupation after restoration, and section 18(1)(iii), which separately covers specified tenants ejected before commencement and imposes a one-year application limit, clause (i) permits the six years to be completed by the application date. The Court found no basis in the Act’s scheme, including sections 9-A and 10-A, to add the proposed restriction. Ganpat v. Jagmal, Amar Singh v. State of Punjab, and Mam Raj v. State of Punjab were distinguished because they concerned different questions.

predicates.tenant_purchase_application_case: A tenant sought, through a purchase application, to acquire land held under the tenancy from the landlord.
predicates.continuous_six_years_by_application: The tenant had occupied the land continuously for at least six years by the time the purchase application was made.
predicates.other_purchase_conditions_satisfied: The tenant met the other conditions applicable to the claimed purchase right.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeking to purchase tenanted land has completed six years of continuous occupation by applying and meets the other conditions, the tenant qualifies under the six-year requirement.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant seeking to purchase land need not have been a tenant of that land when the governing enactment commenced.
material_facts: The landlords disputed purchase claims on the ground that the claimants had to be tenants when the Act commenced.
The Court considered the statutory scheme, which contemplated tenancies beginning after the Act commenced.
The purchase claims were made by tenants applying to purchase land from their landlords.
issues.conclusion: It is not necessary for a tenant claiming under section 18(1)(i) to have been a tenant of the land when the Act commenced, provided the other applicable conditions are satisfied.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(1)(i) does not state that a claimant must have been a tenant when the Act commenced. The Court also relied on the scheme’s recognition that a tenancy could begin after commencement, including the indication in the second proviso to section 9-A. It therefore declined to read a commencement-date tenancy requirement into section 18(1)(i).

predicates.tenant_purchase_application_case: A tenant sought, through a purchase application, to acquire land held under the tenancy from the landlord.
predicates.post_commencement_tenancy_recognized: The governing scheme contemplated a tenancy coming into existence after the enactment commenced.
predicates.other_purchase_conditions_satisfied: The tenant met the other conditions applicable to the claimed purchase right.

issues.definition: If a tenant seeks to purchase land under a scheme that recognizes tenancies beginning after commencement and meets the other conditions, tenancy at commencement is not required.
